key_insight: B-VQE is a variational quantum algorithm that uses separate left/right quantum states plus a biorthogonal objective to efficiently map non-Hermitian phase transitions and exceptional points on NISQ hardware.
engineering_relevance: It offers a hardware-friendly route to simulate open, non-Hermitian many-body systems without costly post-selection, making phase-diagram exploration more practical for quantum devices.
method: Independent variational circuits for left and right eigenstates
Biorthogonal cost function with an Exceptional-Point Detector (EPD)
Non-Hermitian QGT readout and importance-sampling mitigation
evidence_signal: The paper reports noise-free simulations on a non-Hermitian Hubbard chain, XXZ spin chain, and 2D (t)-(J) model, achieving relative energy errors below 5×10^-3 and accurate exceptional-point localization.
watch_item: The approach is validated in simulation, so real-hardware performance may still be limited by noise, circuit depth, and the accuracy of biorthogonal measurements.
paper_title: Exceptional-Point-Anchored Variational Quantum Eigensolver for Non-Hermitian Many-Body Phase Diagrams: Bridging Skin-Effect Topology and Entanglement Criticality on NISQ Hardware
